Definitions: Sample s=(X,R), with X:A->Y and R_a:A\{a}->Y; g_s(a,a)=X(a), g_s(a,b)=R_a(b) for b!=a.; w(s)=product_b q(b,X(b)) times product_a product_{b!=a} q(b,R_a(b)); weights are column-indexed.; C(s)=#{a in A: for every b in A, g_s(a,b)=f(X(b))}.; T_k=sum_{s:C(s)>=k}w(s); B_k=sum_s binom(C(s),k)w(s).
Hypotheses: A and Y are finite.; q:A×Y->R and q(a,y)>=0 for all a,y.; f:Y->Y is arbitrary.
Quantifiers: For every finite A,Y, every nonnegative q and every f:Y->Y. C1 does not explicitly type k; retrieve the intended k in the nonnegative integers, retaining k=0, k>|A| and empty sets.
Conclusion: B_k-k B_{k+1}<=T_k<=B_k. Under intended counting conventions binom(c,0)=1 and binom(c,k)=0 for k>c. No normalization or capture-event independence is assumed.
Related mathematical terms: Bonferroni tail inequalities; binomial moments; factorial moment bounds; at least k events; generalized inclusion-exclusion; finite nonnegative measure; arbitrary event dependence; first lower and upper Bonferroni truncations
